accuracy.evidence: Desert as under about 250 mm precipitation a year checked against National Geographic and USGS desert definitions; Antarctica as a cold desert (very low inland precipitation) and the Gobi at about 194 mm a year from encyclopaedia figures; fennec ears up to about 15 cm and used to lose heat and hear prey (Smithsonian / San Diego Zoo factsheets); camel hump is fat and a thirsty camel can drink about 135 litres in about 13 minutes (National Geographic); kangaroo rats get water from seeds and metabolic water. Burrow temperatures are labelled as a typical example in the adult text.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented primary misconceptions: all deserts are hot and sandy (Antarctica prediction, p1, m1, tag hot), the camel's hump stores water (hump prediction and the water card's feedback, p2, tag hump), big ears keep a fox warm (m7, tag ears, compared with the Arctic fox), burrows must be hotter because enclosed (burrow prediction, m2, tag burrow), and animals that never drink need no water (kangaroo rat prediction, m3, tag drink).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdesert is about heat and water only: five rain gauges filled against a dashed 250 mm line, a fennec fox whose ear tip is dragged up while a 'heat kept in' bar falls, a meerkat dragged down a tunnel past a depth thermometer, fat or water cards dragged into a camel's hump followed by a drinking trough, and five animals matched to their tricks. flagnoc is about night senses and flagsavanna about grassland diets and herds.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each mechanism is seen before it is named: gauges reveal that freezing inland Antarctica and the Gobi fall under the line; the heat bar turns green only once the ears are big; the readout drops from 65 °C to about 30 °C as the meerkat goes deeper; dropping water in the hump is rejected with the fat explanation; a wrong trick says whose trick it is. The step text then confirms.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with a tempting wrong option: Antarctica not a desert 'because deserts are hot and sandy', fox ears 'to keep the sun off its face' or 'to store water', the sand on top being coolest, a hump full of water, and a kangaroo rat 'needing no water'. Each is disproved by the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (what all deserts share, the hump, fox ears, meerkat burrows at midday, kangaroo rat water, when scorpions hunt, why the Gobi is a desert). Wrong options carry tags hot, hump, ears, burrow, drink and hide, each with a message that names the slip.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade about 2.9 and adult 6.5 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0); the long adult paragraph was split after the validator flagged it. Science words habitat, adaptation, nocturnal, burrow, predator and prey are used and explained in plain words.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: deserts are dry, hot or cold; adaptations and the fox's ears; burrows and hiding by day; the hump myth and the kangaroo rat. Adult: NC links and key words, facts with figures, five named mistakes, the lab steps with a note that the temperatures are an example. No filler pattern matched and the overlap gate passed.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light: five gauges fit across 358 px with place names compressed to fit, the 250 mm label got a background after it overlapped a gauge, the fox's ears stay inside the canvas at full size, depth labels sit right of the tunnel, the camel and trough fit, and the five trick rows are 46 px tall. Feedback wraps to at most three lines.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins: 'Measure <place>' for each gauge, 'Bigger ears' / 'Smaller ears', 'Dig deeper' / 'Go up', 'Put fat / water in the hump', 'Drink 45 litres', and one button per trick labelled with the current animal. Canvas aria-label and live region carry every message; walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
